name: DUCHESNE - CRUDE OIL
incident_summary: A waxy crude oil spill resulted from an unlatched top hatch on a transport vehicle, resulting in a spill approximately seven miles long that started in Duchesne at the Main Street and 100 West and concludes on the west side of the bridge over Starvation Reservoir. The crude oil does not flow and is contained to the road. Currently, it has not impacted the soils next to the road, a waterway, a storm drain, or a dry drainage. Utah Highway Patrol is blocking traffic to prevent vehicles from driving through the spill. The volume is currently unknown and the spill is not consistent over the seven miles. The remediation response is in its early stages, with the contractor EMB on scene applying sand for absorption and will likely collect the sand and oil. Further remediation efforts are being evaluated. No injuries have been reported. ______________________________________________________________________________ Update 3/5/2026 at 11 pm - Savage Infrastructure has provided an update. The crude oil only spilled for five blocks west of the intersection of Main Street and 100 West, with some tracked further down the road by vehicles (not spilled from the truck for seven miles as initially reported). There is no oil near the bridge near Starvation Reservoir. The oil has solidified, the widest part of the spill is 8 to 10 feet, and has not reached the edge of the road. There has been no impact to surface water or storm drains. An additional third party remediation company, Enviro Care is enroute, and the project manager is Dirk Haywood, who can be reached at 801-698-8263.

name: UPDATED DUCHESNE - NATURAL GAS RELEASE
incident_summary: From NRC Incident Report # 1431810 and 1431814 on 5/21/25: “The caller reported that they were notified of a fire on a wellhead. The fire was due to a cut in the flex pipe on the wellhead. The fire was extinguished, but there was a release of natural gas into the atmosphere (273.3 MCF). The amount released was less than the reportable quantity. The caller reported that damage estimate is $230,000. The fire was extinguished. An investigation is underway. The wellhead was shut in.” The Duty Officer spoke to the Reporting Party (RP) and obtained updated information from this incident on 5/22/25 at 10:43 AM. The RP stated that the cost estimates for the repairs were received yesterday (5/21), and due to the estimates exceeding $145,000, he was required to report the incident to the NRC. The natural gas release was 273.3 thousand cubic feet, which was well below the reportable threshold of 3.5 million cubic feet (MMcf). The release occurred due to mechanical fatigue in the flex pipe from the wellhead to the gathering line, and the natural gas ignited. The wellhead was shut, the gathering line was isolated, the release ceased, and the Fire Department extinguished the fire. No injuries were reported. The RP will submit a 30-day follow-up report in the PHMSA system. **Update** From NRC Incident Report #1432016 received on 5/23/25 at 17:30. "The incident date is updated to 4/29/2025 and the cause of the incident is due to a crimp fitting on the flex pipe that was installed incorrectly, which caused it to fail over time. The cause is updated to operator error, no other changes or updates." NRC#1432016 is attached.

name: BRIDGELAND - WATER
incident_summary: A break in a transfer line released approximately 6,000 barrels of Duchesne River water to Antelope creek. Prior to entering the transfer line, the water was held in a detention pond after transfer from the Duchesne River. Recently, the line had been used to transport hydrocarbon-free production water. However, any remaining hydrocarbon-free production water would have likely been removed by the approximately 24 hours of transfer of Duchesne River water through the line from the detention pond. It is believed that the released water did not contain hydrocarbon-free production water. Antelope Creek, which is currently dry and about 5 miles from the Duchesne River, received the water. It is estimated the release traveled about 0.75 miles before soaking into the creek bed. The release has been stopped. The water that was released soaked into the dry riverbed of Antelope Creek. An environmental engineering firm is scheduled to take creek bottom and bank samples on December 18, 2024 to confirm the absence of contamination. For more information, contact McCoy Anderson at Outlaw Engineering at 435-823-4320.

incident_summary: From NRC Incident Report # 1411463 on 9/20/24 at 1714 MST: “The caller reported a release of an unknown amount of natural gas from a transfer pipeline that went into the atmosphere at the incident location.
